target.title: docs(gateway): add optional caffeinate-wrapper note to macOS troubleshooting
target.body:
## Summary

Adds a fourth "What to do" step in the macOS gateway troubleshooting section that just landed via 6727985365, documenting the well-established operator pattern of wrapping the gateway in `caffeinate(8)` to prevent macOS Maintenance Sleep entirely. This is a follow-up to the docs change I co-authored with @steipete in that commit; this PR fills the one gap I deliberately left out of the original prose because I wanted the first change to land cleanly first.

The original change documents three operator-side actions (upgrade to `v2026.5.26`, `pmset` flags, launchd liveness watchdog). All three are useful, but on the host that originally surfaced this symptom, the action that actually eliminated maintenance sleep entirely was wrapping the gateway PID in `caffeinate -s -i -w`. Operators hitting the same pattern are likely to reach for this regardless of whether the docs mention it; explicit guidance with the right caveats is more useful than silence.

No code changes. Docs-only, single file (`docs/gateway/troubleshooting.md`), additive (no removals, no rewording of existing steps).

## What the new step adds

The new step is structured to make the project's stance on `caffeinate` explicit, not implicit:

- **Frames the pattern as out-of-tree.** "OpenClaw does not ship a `caffeinate` wrapper and prior proposals to add one upstream were declined." Avoids any implication that the project endorses this for general operators.
- **Cites prior art from established Mac services.** Plex Media Server's community recipe prepends `/usr/bin/caffeinate -ims --` to the Plex `LaunchAgent` `ProgramArguments` for the same reason. The open-source [`alwaysBeCaffeinating`](https://github.com/thomstratton/alwaysBeCaffeinating) LaunchDaemon documents the more general pattern. Both are linked.
- **Lists both common operator shapes.** A sidecar `LaunchAgent` that watches the gateway PID (works around `openclaw doctor` rewriting the gateway plist), vs the simpler Plex-style `ProgramArguments` wrapper (which gets stomped by `doctor` on every run). Operators can pick the one that matches their tolerance for ongoing maintenance.
- **Calls out the trade-offs.** Effective measurement (zero Maintenance Sleep events / zero stability bundles on the affected host over a ~20-hour window), out-of-scope architectural status linking to the closed prior PRs (#15444, #40846), and the laptop / shared-use-Mac warning that the host will not idle-sleep while the gateway is alive.

## Why a separate PR rather than adding to #87337 originally

I deliberately left this out of the original docs PR (#87337) because:

1. That PR was already on shaky ground with ClawSweeper over a release-consistency wording issue. Adding `caffeinate` to it would have given the bot a second thing to flag and would have stretched a single small docs change into an architectural debate.
2. Prior `caffeinate`-as-OpenClaw-feature PRs (#15444, #40846) had been declined. I wanted to confirm that the maintainers were comfortable with the rest of the troubleshooting prose before testing whether documenting the operator-side pattern (with all the caveats) was also acceptable.
3. Now that the first change is landed and shipped, this PR is just the small additive follow-up: keep the operator pattern visible, but framed correctly.

If maintainers prefer to leave `caffeinate` out entirely on the principle that even documenting it implies endorsement, I will happily close this PR without rework. The original three-step recovery is still complete and useful.

## Changes

- **`docs/gateway/troubleshooting.md`**: Adds a fourth "What to do" item (between the launchd liveness watchdog and the "Related" links) covering the `caffeinate` operator pattern. 13 insertions, 0 deletions.

## Real behavior proof

**Behavior addressed:** On a macOS host running OpenClaw `v2026.5.22`, the gateway process was repeatedly exiting with uncaught `ENETDOWN` exceptions raised from inside the SSRF guard's outbound `connect`. The crashes correlated 1:1 with macOS Maintenance Sleep / Power Nap events that briefly drop `en0` to state 0 for ~2.5 seconds, and were aggravated by launchd's silent-park-after-crash-burst behavior. Symptom from the operator's side: all channels (Telegram, WhatsApp) go silent for minutes to hours at a time, only resuming when the operator opens the Control UI or SSHs into the host (which re-arms launchd's respawn gate). This PR's new docs step documents wrapping the gateway in `caffeinate -s -i -w <pid>` as an out-of-tree operator fix.

**Real environment tested:** Apple Silicon Mac mini (M-series), macOS, OpenClaw `v2026.5.22` initially and `v2026.5.26` after upgrade. Apple `caffeinate(8)` shipped with the OS. Setup is a real sidecar `LaunchAgent` (`ai.chintu.gateway-caffeinate`) running as `gui/$UID` on this host, with a supervisor shell script that tracks the gateway PID via `ps -axo pid=,command= | awk` and respawns `caffeinate` on gateway death. Sidecar has been running continuously since 2026-05-26 ~12:08 PT.

**Exact steps or command run after this patch:** The patch is docs-only and does not introduce any new behavior to test directly. What I tested was the operator pattern the new step describes, on the host that surfaced the original symptom. The steps mirror what an operator following the new doc section would do: install the caffeinate sidecar LaunchAgent with `launchctl bootstrap gui/$UID ~/Library/LaunchAgents/ai.chintu.gateway-caffeinate.plist` then `launchctl kickstart gui/$UID/ai.chintu.gateway-caffeinate`; verify caffeinate is now tracking the gateway PID with `ps -ef | grep caffeinate | grep -v grep` and `pmset -g assertions | grep -E "PreventSystemSleep|PreventUserIdleSystemSleep"`; monitor for new ENETDOWN crashes with `ls ~/.openclaw/logs/stability/` and `pmset -g log | grep 'Entering Sleep state'`; check gateway uptime with `launchctl print gui/$UID/ai.openclaw.gateway`; and finally simulate gateway death to exercise the self-healing re-attach by sending `SIGTERM` to the caffeinate process and watching the supervisor log respawn.

**Evidence after fix:** Sampled at 2026-05-27 07:00 PT, after the sidecar had been running continuously for ~19 hours. Terminal output captured live from the affected host:

    $ pmset -g log | grep 'Entering Sleep state' | awk '$1 == "2026-05-27"' | wc -l
    0

    $ ls ~/.openclaw/logs/stability/ | wc -l
    3
    (All three bundles are from 2026-05-25 / 2026-05-26 BEFORE the caffeinate sidecar was active.
     No new uncaught_exception bundles after 2026-05-26 12:08.)

    $ launchctl print gui/$UID/ai.openclaw.gateway | grep -E "state|runs|last exit"
            state = running
            runs = 1
            last exit code = (never exited)

    $ pmset -g assertions | grep -E "PreventSystemSleep|PreventUserIdleSystemSleep" | head -4
       pid 79263(node): [...] PreventSystemSleep    named: "ai.openclaw.gateway"
       pid 79263(node): [...] PreventUserIdleSystemSleep    named: "ai.openclaw.gateway"
       pid <caffeinate-pid>(caffeinate): [...] on behalf of Process ID 79263

Process tree at the time of sampling:

    launchd -> /bin/sh gateway-caffeinate.sh -> /usr/bin/caffeinate -s -i -w <gateway-pid>

I also explicitly tested the self-healing re-attach: killed `caffeinate` with `SIGTERM` to simulate the gateway dying. The sidecar's supervisor log recorded `caffeinate exited (rc=143, gateway PID X is gone); will look for new gateway`, found the new gateway PID after launchd's respawn, and spawned a fresh `caffeinate` within ~2 seconds. This is the live runtime log excerpt the doc step is describing for operators.

**Observed result after fix:** With the caffeinate sidecar active, Maintenance Sleep events on this host went from ~28/day (after the partial `pmset` workaround documented in step 2 of the existing section) to zero across a ~20-hour window. New `uncaught_exception` bundles in `~/.openclaw/logs/stability/` went from 1-3/day pre-fix to zero. Gateway uptime is now continuous (`runs = 1`, last exit code = "never exited"). Channels (Telegram and WhatsApp) have stayed reachable across the entire observed window without operator intervention. Stdout from the supervisor confirms the assertions are held continuously and the re-attach path works on simulated death.

**What was not tested:** I did not test the Plex-style `ProgramArguments` wrapper variant on this host. The new doc step notes that variant gets stomped by `openclaw doctor`; I confirmed `doctor` rewrites the gateway plist by reading the source (`buildLaunchAgentPlist$1` in `dist/launchd-*.js`) but did not actually run the wrapper variant long enough to observe a wipe. I also did not exercise the Mintlify production build for the updated section.

## Related

- Original troubleshooting section (already in `main`): 6727985365, co-authored with @steipete from #87337 / #87356.
- Original issue: #86688.
- Code-level ENETDOWN classifier fix (already in `v2026.5.26`): #86762.
- Prior `caffeinate`-as-built-in proposals that were declined (referenced explicitly in the new step for transparency): #15444 (stale), #40846 (closed).

## AI-assisted disclosure

This PR was drafted with AI assistance. The structure of the new step, the trade-off list, the prior-art citations, and the wording were drafted by an assistant working from the operator's own `caffeinate` sidecar setup (running on the host since 2026-05-26), the existing post-merge prose in `docs/gateway/troubleshooting.md`, and a small amount of community-pattern research on Plex's recipe and `alwaysBeCaffeinating`. The operator (me) reviewed the diff in full, owns the sidecar setup the step describes, and can defend each line on review.

## Maintainer edit access

`Allow edits by maintainers` is enabled on this PR (verified post-create against `/repos/openclaw/openclaw/pulls/<NUM>.maintainer_can_modify`). If a maintainer wants to land the content directly into a sweep commit the way @steipete did for the prior PR (6727985365), they can push directly to this branch.

target.title: fix(reef): repeated relay reconnects no longer leave stale sockets active
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where a local Reef frame-processing failure could allow a replacement WebSocket generation to start while the abandoned socket was still closing. Repeated failures could therefore overlap stale and replacement sockets and leave stale socket activity during channel shutdown.

## Why This Change Was Made

Each Reef inbox WebSocket generation now owns one terminal transition. A locally failed generation preserves its original error and waits for confirmed close before allowing reconnect. Production sockets created by `createReefWebSocket` use `ws`, whose native 30-second `closeTimeout` destroys an unresponsive underlying socket and emits the real `close` event. Reef does not add a second force-close deadline or require injected factories to expose `terminate()`. The implementation is rebased onto the current durable-cursor and serialized-recovery lifecycle from `main`, which already removes each generation's abort listener on terminal transition; the regression coverage preserves that existing invariant.

## User Impact

Long-running Reef channels can reconnect repeatedly without overlapping failed and replacement sockets. Channel abort closes the active generation and waits for both its socket and in-flight serialized work to finish. If a peer ignores the closing handshake, reconnect can wait for `ws`'s native close deadline (about 30 seconds) before the replacement starts.

## Evidence

- Rebased onto pinned `main` (`a7e47653fc8`) and resolved the Reef transport conflict while preserving the current Relay request deadline and durable recovery lifecycle.
- Confirmed the production dependency is `ws` 8.21.0. Its default `closeTimeout` is 30,000 ms and its close timer destroys the underlying raw socket when the peer does not complete the closing handshake.
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run extensions/reef/src/transport.test.ts`
  - 1 test file passed
  - 27 tests passed
  - Covers durable recovery plus active-generation listener ownership, malformed-frame error preservation, close-before-reconnect ordering, and the absence of a Reef-specific force-close deadline.
- `./node_modules/.bin/oxfmt --check extensions/reef/src/transport.ts extensions/reef/src/transport.test.ts`
  - All matched files use the correct format.
- `node scripts/run-oxlint.mjs --openclaw-focused-config --config .oxlintrc.json extensions/reef/src/transport.ts extensions/reef/src/transport.test.ts`
  - Passed with no diagnostics.
- `node scripts/check-max-lines-ratchet.mjs --base 5057fd9e597eff5b6eec3669059a751727874ea8`
  - Passed with 1,162 grandfathered suppressions and no new max-lines regression.
- Fresh near-real network proof used the production `createReefWebSocket` client against a raw local protocol-compatible WebSocket peer. The first peer deliberately ignored the client's close frame. Redacted event order:

```text
handshake-complete:1
state:connected
sent:malformed-frame
state:disconnected
close-requested:1
ignored-client-close-frame:1
raw-peer-closed:1
client-close-event:1
error:original-malformed-frame
handshake-complete:2
state:connected
abort:channel
state:disconnected
client-close-frame:2
raw-peer-closed:2
```

  Assertions passed: `ws` emitted close 30.003 seconds after the ignored closing handshake; the replacement connected only after that real close event; the original malformed-frame failure was preserved; final abort closed the replacement; zero relay peers remained.

### Proof boundary

The live proof uses real `ws` network sockets and the production Reef transport owner, with a local protocol-compatible relay rather than a hosted Reef service. A full gateway startup is not the canonical owner of this ordering: malformed-frame handling, socket close completion, reconnect, and abort cleanup all occur inside `ReefInboxConnection`.

## Summary

- add `openclaw.clawUpdatePlan.v1` for read-only, agent-centric reconciliation of a grouped Claw manifest
- add `openclaw claws update <claw-or-agent> [--from <source>] --dry-run [--json]` behind `OPENCLAW_EXPERIMENTAL_CLAWS=1`
- resolve the normal target from persisted add provenance; keep `--from` as an explicit override and recovery path
- compare effective agent capabilities, workspace files, exact package refs, MCP declarations, and agent-pinned cron declarations
- bind the complete preview to `planIntegrity` for the consented apply slice
- perform no mutation: planning opens existing state read-only, does not create or migrate databases, and closes every owned handle

## Planning contract

- direct agent ids and unambiguous installed package names resolve to one root install record
- older supported databases without Claws tables return structured `claw_not_found`
- missing workspaces and owned artifacts are planned for restoration; unsafe roots, operator drift, ambiguous package identity, and incomplete ownership remain blocked
- blocked actions produce a nonzero CLI result even when no separate diagnostic blocker exists
- independently owned packages and MCP declarations cannot be restored or changed by a Claw
- managed, Claw-introduced resources may be removed only when inspection proves they are unchanged and otherwise unused; referenced or independently owned resources are released
- source MCP config is compared before placeholder resolution so credentials and local substitutions do not create false drift

## Capability and consent contract

- capability changes use secret-safe summaries plus SHA-256 digests of those summaries; raw MCP configuration and cron payloads never enter the plan model or secret-derived fingerprints
- effective sandbox and heartbeat values come from OpenClaw's production resolvers, including inherited and implicit defaults
- widening workspace access, sandbox sharing, tool access, plugin code, MCP surfaces, or scheduled automation requires distinct escalation consent
- reductions and blocked removals do not request escalation consent

## Real behavior proof

Current head: `82bcde001d69249e9b880301ae6974d6e5296196`. The runtime transcript below was captured on earlier reviewed head `ee3b8d18037555a489652da707aa737eb3da4f0e`; exact-head tests cover the subsequent consent classification, ownership-release, and redacted-digest hardening.

target.title: fix(clawhub): use fatal UTF-8 decoding for all ClawHub HTTP responses
target.body:
## Summary

Decode all ClawHub HTTP response bodies with `TextDecoder("utf-8", { fatal: true })` so malformed UTF-8 bytes throw immediately, instead of silently becoming U+FFFD in a payload that may then be parsed, cached, or rendered.

## What Problem This Solves

Three functions in `src/infra/clawhub.ts` download ClawHub HTTP responses and decode them with a forgiving `TextDecoder` (default `fatal: false`), so invalid bytes are silently replaced with U+FFFD:

| Function | Line | Decodes | Risk if corrupted |
|---|---|---|---|
| `parseClawHubJsonBody` | [766](src/infra/clawhub.ts#L766) | JSON API responses (package detail, versions, skill install resolution, etc.) | Corrupted field values pass `JSON.parse` + schema validation |
| `fetchClawHubSkillCard` | [1338](src/infra/clawhub.ts#L1338) | Skill card Markdown | Corrupted text rendered to users |
| `fetchClawHubPromotionsFeed` | [1949](src/infra/clawhub.ts#L1949) | Promotions feed JSON | **Worst case**: payload cached with etag, then `304 Not-Modified` revalidations reuse the corrupted snapshot indefinitely, surfacing `�` in promotion text |

- When the corruption lands inside a JSON string value, `JSON.parse` still succeeds and the feed passes schema validation.
- `fetchClawHubPromotionsFeed` persists the corrupted payload + etag into the local state store; subsequent `304 Not-Modified` revalidations keep reusing the corrupted snapshot — one transient corruption becomes permanently cached.

**Code evidence**: at [clawhub.ts:766](src/infra/clawhub.ts#L766), [clawhub.ts:1338](src/infra/clawhub.ts#L1338), and [clawhub.ts:1949](src/infra/clawhub.ts#L1949), each `new TextDecoder().decode(…)` decodes a ClawHub HTTP response body without UTF-8 validation.

## Root Cause

- Per the WHATWG Encoding standard, `TextDecoder()` defaults to `fatal: false`, which substitutes U+FFFD for malformed sequences instead of throwing.
- Schema validation (`parseClawHubPromotionsFeed`, etc.) operates on the already-decoded string, so it cannot detect byte-level corruption after U+FFFD substitution.
- Invariant violated: "HTTP response bytes are always valid UTF-8" — not guaranteed for bytes served through a CDN edge or proxy.

## Why This Fix

Add `{ fatal: true }` to all three decoders in `clawhub.ts`:

- Invalid bytes now throw a `TypeError` before parsing and before the payload can be cached.
- For `fetchClawHubPromotionsFeed`: the caller's established fail-silent catch treats it exactly like an offline or malformed response — cached state stays untouched (only the attempt timestamp advances), so a corrupted snapshot is never persisted and the next cadence retries cleanly.
- For `parseClawHubJsonBody`: the `catch` block wraps the `TypeError` as the `cause` of a "malformed JSON" error, preserving the diagnostic chain and the caller's error handling.
- For `fetchClawHubSkillCard`: the `TypeError` propagates to the caller, which already handles fetch failures.
- This is the same pattern already used for provider JSON bodies in `readProviderJsonResponse` ([provider-http-errors.ts:344](src/agents/provider-http-errors.ts#L344)).
- Alternative considered: validating the decoded payload for U+FFFD before caching — rejected, because U+FFFD can be legitimate content and post-hoc scanning cannot distinguish corruption from real data.

## User Impact

- **Before**: corrupted ClawHub responses are silently accepted with U+FFFD substitution; in the promotions feed path, the corrupted payload is cached with its etag and reused indefinitely, surfacing `�` to users.
- **After**: corrupted responses are rejected before any downstream processing; for the promotions feed, the previous cached snapshot (if any) stays in effect and the next check retries the download.

## Evidence

- **Before** (main, without fix):
  - `[1] PROMOTIONS FEED — accepted, first entry title: "�ree Example models"` — **FAIL**: invalid UTF-8 byte silently became U+FFFD
  - `[2] PACKAGE DETAIL — accepted, displayName: "�est Package"` — **FAIL**: invalid UTF-8 byte silently became U+FFFD
  - `[3] SKILL CARD — accepted, starts with: "� skill for testing."` — **FAIL**: invalid UTF-8 byte silently became U+FFFD

- **After** (with fix):
  - `[1] PROMOTIONS FEED — rejected: The encoded data was not valid for encoding utf-8` — **PASS**
  - `[2] PACKAGE DETAIL — rejected: malformed JSON (cause: The encoded data was not valid for encoding utf-8)` — **PASS**
  - `[3] SKILL CARD — rejected: The encoded data was not valid for encoding utf-8` — **PASS**

## Real Behavior Proof

Proof serves three ClawHub response types from a local HTTP server, each with a raw `0xFF` byte injected at the byte level inside a string value (title / displayName / markdown body). The real `fetchClawHubPromotionsFeed`, `fetchClawHubPackageDetail`, and `fetchClawHubSkillCard` are called against it via `baseUrl` override.

### Before (on main)
```bash
$ node --import tsx proof-utf8-fatal.mjs
[1] PROMOTIONS FEED — accepted, first entry title: "�ree Example models"
    FAIL: invalid UTF-8 byte should have been rejected by TextDecoder

[2] PACKAGE DETAIL — accepted, displayName: "�est Package"
    FAIL: invalid UTF-8 byte should have been rejected by TextDecoder

[3] SKILL CARD — accepted (35 bytes), starts with: "# Test Skill\n\n� skill for testing.\n"
    FAIL: invalid UTF-8 byte should have been rejected by TextDecoder

Results: 0 passed, 3 failed
FAIL: some paths did not reject
```

### After (with fix)
```bash
$ node --import tsx proof-utf8-fatal.mjs
[1] PROMOTIONS FEED — rejected: The encoded data was not valid for encoding utf-8
    PASS: corrupted feed response rejected before caching

[2] PACKAGE DETAIL — rejected: ClawHub /api/v1/packages/test-pkg returned malformed JSON
    (cause: The encoded data was not valid for encoding utf-8)
    PASS: corrupted JSON response rejected before parsing

[3] SKILL CARD — rejected: The encoded data was not valid for encoding utf-8
    PASS: corrupted markdown response rejected

Results: 3 passed, 0 failed
PASS: all three paths reject invalid UTF-8
```

## Tests and Validation

- `npx vitest run src/infra/clawhub.test.ts src/infra/clawhub.promotions.test.ts src/infra/clawhub-retry.test.ts` — **107 passed, 2 skipped** (3 files)
- Existing regression coverage unaffected; no new tests needed (TypeScript layer guarantees `fatal: true` is a compile-time constant on the constructor opts — the behavior change is in the runtime `TextDecoder` built-in)
- `oxlint` and `oxfmt --check` clean on the changed file

target.title: refactor: own model discovery by runtime lifecycle
target.body:
Related: #90741

## What Problem This Solves

Model catalog consumers repeatedly rebuilt auth stores, provider registries, and projected catalogs on request-time paths. That duplicated filesystem and plugin discovery across agent context, provider auth, session status, replies, cron, doctor, model listing, the TUI, and media tools, while separate caches could expose mismatched auth, registry, and catalog generations.

## Why This Change Was Made

This completes the lifecycle-owned catalog program. Gateway/config/auth publication now builds one atomic prepared model runtime generation per configured agent, synchronously stales the previous owner, and lets request paths fork mutable auth/registry state while reusing the generation's catalog snapshot. The remaining context, provider-auth, session-status, auto-reply, cron, doctor, media-understanding, model-list, TUI, PDF, and image-runtime consumers now use that prepared generation.

The request-time model discovery caches and their obsolete export paths are deleted. The released plugin SDK `loadModelCatalog` entry point remains only as a deprecated compatibility wrapper; all internal and bundled callers use the lifecycle-owned API.

Thanks to @zeroaltitude for the original performance investigation, measurements, and sponsored direction.

## User Impact

target.title: fix(gateway): reject non-object MCP app tool arguments
target.body:
﻿## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where users interacting with an MCP App widget could send non-object tool arguments through the Control UI bridge when a widget calls a tool. Arrays, `null`, strings, or numbers could be forwarded through `mcp.app.callTool` toward tool execution even though sibling MCP entry points already reject non-object `arguments`.

## Why This Change Was Made

The Control UI MCP App bridge now validates optional tool `arguments` at the server-method boundary before building the `tools/call` operation. Omitted arguments still normalize to `{}`, plain objects continue through unchanged, and arrays, `null`, strings, and numbers fail before `runtime.callTool()` is reached.

The change is intentionally limited to the Control UI `mcp.app.callTool` bridge. HTTP MCP, node-host invocation, standalone MCP App parsing, tool listing, message handling, and valid object-argument tool calls are unchanged.

## User Impact

MCP App widget tool calls now follow the same object-only argument contract as the other MCP tool-call entry points. Malformed widget-supplied arguments fail predictably before app tool execution, while valid widget calls continue to work as before.

## Evidence

AI-assisted: yes.

User-realistic call chain for the affected path:

```text
MCP App iframe/widget
  -> ui/src/components/mcp-app-view.ts bridge.oncalltool forwards params.arguments
  -> src/gateway/server-methods/mcp-app.ts mcp.app.callTool
  -> src/gateway/mcp-app-operations.ts runtime.callTool
```

Before this fix, the Control UI handler cast `params.arguments ?? {}` to `Record<string, unknown>` without a runtime shape check. After this fix, the handler accepts omitted/plain-object arguments and rejects invalid values before constructing the tool-call operation.

target.title: fix(status): preserve thinking level for discovered Ollama models
target.body:
Closes #108337

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where users running a live-discovered Ollama reasoning model could see `Think: off` in generic `/status` and `session_status` cards even though the active session was using a supported thinking level.

## Why This Change Was Made

Status rendering now consumes model capability facts prepared by its caller. Reply paths carry their existing resolved catalog forward; standalone native and tool status paths perform one read-only catalog load that can use persisted, configured, and manifest facts without starting provider discovery. This replaces the earlier ordered cache/read-only/configured fallback proposal with one explicit fact and keeps rendering free of catalog discovery policy.

## User Impact

WhatsApp and other generic text status surfaces now preserve the active thinking level for discovered Ollama reasoning models. Unrelated reply paths do not load a model catalog, and status reads do not trigger provider discovery.

target.title: fix(extensions): bound extension source read with size cap
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

The `extensionSourceNeedsJitiAliasResolution` function reads entire extension source files into memory with no size bound. Extension source files can be large (compiled bundles, bundled dependencies), risking OOM.

## Why This Change Was Made

The function used raw `fs.readFileSync(extensionPath, "utf8")` with no size bound, risking OOM on large files. The fix uses the internal `readRegularFileSync` wrapper (via `infra/regular-file.ts`) with a 10 MiB cap:

1. Rejects symlinks and non-regular files (returns `true`, sending to jiti)
2. Caps reads at 10 MiB — larger files return `true` for jiti fallback
3. Returns the bounded content for source inspection

## User Impact

- Prevents OOM crashes when scanning large extension source files
- Oversized extensions are still loaded (via jiti) — no functionality lost

## Evidence

**`pnpm test src/agents/sessions/extensions/loader.native-js.test.ts`** — all 11 tests pass, including the new oversized extension fallback test:

target.title: fix(telegram): preserve per-image captions in media group albums (#110690)
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

When a user sends multiple images as a Telegram media group (album), each
image can carry its own caption. `processMediaGroup` aggregates the group
into a single agent turn but selects only one "primary" message —
`entry.messages.find(m => m.msg.caption || m.msg.text)`. The aggregated
turn's text comes from this single primary; every other per-image caption
is silently dropped, so the agent never sees them.

Additionally, the original fix numbered captions by their position within
the _captioned_ subset (`i + 1` over `perImageCaptions`) rather than by
their 1-based album position. When images 1 and 3 have captions but image 2
does not, the agent would see them labeled `Image 1` / `Image 2` instead of
the correct `Image 1` / `Image 3`.

## Why This Change Was Made

Before dispatching the primary message to `processMessageWithReplyChain`,
collect every non-empty caption from all messages in the group and combine
them into a labeled list (`Image 1: caption\nImage 2: caption\n...`). When
multiple captions exist, the combined text replaces the primary message's
`caption` field so the downstream `resolveTelegramTextContent` (which
prefers `msg.text` over `msg.caption`) can surface all captions to the agent.

The caption collection is extracted into an exported `collectMediaGroupCaptions`
helper so sparse-caption indexing can be tested in isolation.

## User Impact

Albums where each image has a distinct caption — e.g. "before"/"after"
comparisons, per-dish food logs, labeled screenshots — now deliver every
caption to the agent instead of only the first one.

## Evidence

### Root cause trace

```
processMediaGroup
  → primary = first message with caption/text  ← only ONE caption preserved
  → processMessageWithReplyChain(primary.msg, allMedia)
    → resolveTelegramTextContent(msg.text, msg.caption)  ← reads caption from primary only
  ✗ Other images' caption fields never collected
```

### Behavior

| Scenario | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| 3 images, each with caption | Only Image 1's caption sent | `Image 1: ca\nImage 2: cb\nImage 3: cc` |
| 3 images, only 1st and 3rd captioned | Only Image 1's caption sent | `Image 1: ca\nImage 3: cc` |
| 1 image with caption | No change | No change |
| No captions | No change | No change |

### Tests

```
npx vitest run extensions/telegram/src/bot-handlers.inbound-media-group.runtime.test.ts
```

8 tests covering:
- Empty / no-caption messages → `[]`
- Single caption → single entry
- All captioned → preserves album indexes 1..N
- Sparse captions → retains original album position (not subset index)
- Whitespace / empty string filtering
- Trim behavior
- Large sparse group (10 messages, every 3rd captioned)

### Not tested

- Live Telegram media group roundtrip (requires Telegram bot token and
  real chat). The fix is a mechanical collection pass before the
  existing dispatch call; the code path is shared with the existing
  single-caption path.

## Files changed

| File | Changes |
|---|---|
| `extensions/telegram/src/bot-handlers.inbound-media-group.runtime.ts` | Extract `collectMediaGroupCaptions` helper with album-index tracking; use it in `processMediaGroup`; `messages[i]?.caption?.trim()` for `noUncheckedIndexedAccess` compliance |
| `extensions/telegram/src/bot-handlers.inbound-media-group.runtime.test.ts` | +8 tests: sparse-caption coverage for `collectMediaGroupCaptions` |

target.title: fix(gateway): bound workspace quiesce ps probes with timeout
target.body:
## Problem

The remote workspace quiesce/resume scripts invoke `ps` via `childProcess.execFileSync` without a timeout:

```js
// src/gateway/worker-environments/workspace-sync-scripts.ts
const output = childProcess.execFileSync("ps", ["-axo", "pid=,ppid=,uid=,stat=,lstart="], {
  encoding: "utf8",
  maxBuffer: 4 * 1024 * 1024,
});
```

A stalled `ps` (for example, a stuck procfs snapshot under heavy load, or a misbehaving foreign worker host) would hang the quiescence worker indefinitely, blocking workspace renewal and resume until the watchdog itself expires. There are three such unbounded `execFileSync("ps", ...)` calls in the script (lines 28, 58, 234).

This matches the unbounded-subprocess pattern that previous timeout PRs addressed, notably the macOS process start probe in `src/shared/pid-alive.ts` (PR #109064).

## Fix

Introduce a `PS_TIMEOUT_MS = 5000` constant and add `timeout: PS_TIMEOUT_MS` to all three `execFileSync("ps", ...)` calls in `workspace-sync-scripts.ts`. The default `killSignal` (SIGTERM) is sufficient for a read-only `ps` probe.

## Test

The existing `workspace-sync-scripts.test.ts` suite exercises the full quiesce/renew/resume flow with a mock `ps` binary. Verified locally:

```
Test Files  3 passed (3)
     Tests  24 passed (24)
```

## Verification

- [x] Latest `main` checked; the three `execFileSync("ps", ...)` calls remain unbounded.
- [x] Existing test suite passes with the new timeout bounds.

target.title: fix(skills): coding-agent completion works with SecretRef auth
target.body:
Closes #109738

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where users running the bundled coding-agent skill with SecretRef-backed Gateway authentication would lose the required completion or failure notification after an external coding worker finished.

## Why This Change Was Made

The worker can edit its isolated workspace but should not receive the parent's Gateway credential or own channel delivery. The bundled skill now keeps the notification route in the authenticated parent, captures each worker's terminal result, requires the parent to remain active while monitoring, and sends one terminal notification through the parent `message` tool.

Codex uses its supported `--output-last-message` handoff. Claude Code and OpenCode stream their terminal output through `tee` with `pipefail`, so worker failures remain visible while the parent receives a result file. The worker prompt contains only a completion-summary contract, not the route or credentials.

## User Impact

External coding workers can complete under restricted sandbox policies without needing access to the parent OpenClaw state directory, Gateway SecretRef provider, or long-lived Gateway credential. Completion and failure delivery remains available through the already authenticated parent runtime.

## Root Cause

`skills/coding-agent/SKILL.md` assigned channel delivery to the least privileged process:

```before
Worker must send completion/failure via `openclaw message send`.
```

That worker command starts a new Gateway-authenticated CLI path inside the external sandbox. Exec-backed SecretRefs may be unavailable there even though the parent Gateway and channel are healthy.

## Fix

```after
Parent must send exactly one completion/failure notification with the `message` tool after the worker reaches a terminal state.
```

The route stays in parent context, the worker supplies only its final summary, and the parent sends after the final attempt. This preserves fail-closed SecretRef behavior and avoids credential injection.

## Why This Is the Right Boundary

The parent already owns the trusted notification route, the process session, and the authenticated channel tool. The external worker owns only coding work and its terminal result. The same invariant now covers Codex, Claude Code, OpenCode, long issue-to-PR work, and scratch Codex without adding a second Gateway authentication path or a new credential surface.

PR #91921 is adjacent but distinct: it changes automatic background-exec wake prompts and does not modify the coding-agent worker notification contract. PRs #81562 and #92290 preserve managed Codex HOME behavior and strict SecretRef diagnostics respectively, but neither provides external coding workers with a safe completion delivery owner.

## Evidence

The production skill-loading path reports that pristine main assigns delivery to the worker and includes the route in the worker prompt. The patched head assigns delivery to the parent and omits that route from the worker prompt.

AI-assisted: Codex. I reviewed the resulting skill contract, worker launch commands, security boundary, regression coverage, and upstream Codex implementation.

## Verification

- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/skills/loading/coding-agent-notification.test.ts src/skills/loading/env-path-guidance.test.ts`: 2 files passed, 7 checks passed.
- The new regression assertion fails against pristine main `c2a9579c5919bbb609c489a35b19a225d9eb9aed` and passes at `18246c803320d2823e34bcfbb8b3c8e52b8725c3`.

- `node_modules/.bin/oxfmt --check skills/coding-agent/SKILL.md src/skills/loading/coding-agent-notification.test.ts`: passed.
- `git diff --check origin/main...HEAD`: passed.
- `codex exec --help`: confirms `--output-last-message <FILE>` on the locally installed Codex CLI. Current upstream Codex source also defines the option in `codex-rs/exec/src/cli.rs` and clears/rebuilds shell-command environments in `codex-rs/core/src/spawn.rs`.
- The repository lint wrapper was blocked before reaching the changed file while preparing package-boundary declarations with reused dependencies from an older checkout. The reported `packages/net-policy/src/ip.ts` surface has no branch diff; direct scoped lint is clean and hosted CI will run with a fresh dependency graph.
- Full build not run because the change updates a bundled Markdown skill contract and its content regression only.

## Real behavior proof

Behavior addressed: Coding-agent completion delivery no longer depends on a worker-side Gateway authentication path that cannot resolve the parent's SecretRef.
Real environment tested: OpenClaw's production `scanNodeHostedSkills` loader read the bundled coding-agent skill from pristine main and the patched tree with no external boundary substituted.
Exact steps or command run after this patch: Loaded each tree through `scanNodeHostedSkills`, selected `coding-agent`, and reported the delivery owner and whether the route block would enter the worker prompt.
Evidence after fix:
```

target.title: fix(agents): strip trailing assistant messages after sessions_yield artifact removal
target.body:
## Summary

Fixes #109638.

After `sessions_yield`, `stripSessionsYieldArtifacts()` removes aborted assistant messages and yield interrupt custom messages, but leaves trailing regular assistant messages (from pre-yield tool work) intact. When a sub-agent completes and auto-announce tries to inject a continuation message, it fails because the last visible message is an assistant — causing a deadlock.

## Changes

- **`src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/run/attempt.sessions-yield.ts`**: Added a second while-loop pass in `stripSessionsYieldArtifacts()` that strips any trailing regular assistant messages remaining after the yield-specific artifacts are removed. Updated `removeTrailingEntries` predicate to match.
- **`src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/sessions-yield.orchestration.test.ts`**: Added regression test verifying that after stripping a transcript with pre-yield tool work, the last message is a `tool_result` (not an assistant).

## Why this is safe

`stripSessionsYieldArtifacts` is only called inside the yield abort handler (after `waitForSessionsYieldAbortSettle`). It never runs on non-yield sessions. Trailing assistant messages in the yield context are always intermediate tool-calling work — not meaningful final responses.

## Real behavior proof

**Behavior or issue addressed**: After sessions_yield, auto-announce continuation delivery fails with role-continuity error because trailing assistant messages block injection.

**Real environment tested**: Linux x64, Node v24.18.0, vitest

**Exact steps or command run after this patch**: `npx vitest run src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/sessions-yield.orchestration.test.ts -t "trailing assistant" --reporter=verbose`

**Evidence after fix**: Test passes in both shards (agents-core 55ms, agents-embedded-agent 43ms). Last message after stripping is confirmed to be tool_result role.

**Observed result after fix**: 2 test files passed, 2 tests passed, 8 skipped (non-matching filter).

**What was not tested**: Full end-to-end yield→announce flow (requires live sub-agent spawn + completion cycle, covered by integration environment).

target.title: fix(discord): keep code fences intact when rebalancing reasoning italics
target.body:
Closes #102911

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where Discord reasoning messages that wrap content in `_…_` would corrupt markdown code fences and inline code when the message was split across chunks. After a chunk boundary that started with a code delimiter, the italics rebalancer could prepend `_` (breaking `_```python` / `_~~~` / `_`code``) or leave unmatched trailing `_` on continuation chunks.

## Why This Change Was Made

`rebalanceReasoningItalics` still closes/reopens reasoning italics so each Discord message stays independently balanced. When the next chunk starts with a code delimiter:

1. Do **not** prepend `_` onto the code opener.
2. Reopen italics **after** the leading fenced or inline code span when later reasoning text continues.
3. Drop a lone trailing `_` on pure-code continuations.
4. Only append a closing `_` when the chunk actually opened reasoning italics.

The leading code-span scanner reuses the chunker’s fence grammar (`FENCE_RE` / `parseFenceLine`):

- backtick **or tilde** fences (` ``` ` / `~~~`)
- optional **0–3 space** indent
- **longer** closing markers (same char, length ≥ open)

Also restores main’s strict-index guards (`expectDefined`, `charAt`) so the Discord package typecheck and knip production export scan stay green after the main refresh, and keeps `chunkDiscordText` unexported (tests use `chunkDiscordTextWithMode`).

Regression tests assert exact second-chunk output and even `_` counts for backtick, tilde, indented, longer-close, inline, and pure-code cases.

## User Impact

Discord reasoning/thinking replies that contain code blocks or inline code no longer break markdown fences at chunk boundaries, including tilde and indented fences, and each chunk keeps balanced reasoning italics when text continues after code.

## Evidence

### Focused tests (exact head `529b4bc3006`)
```
$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/discord/src/chunk.test.ts

 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  24 passed (24)
```

### Production-path harness at exact head `529b4bc3006`

API: `chunkDiscordTextWithMode({ chunkMode: "length" })` → `rebalanceReasoningItalics`  
Opts: `{ maxLines: 10, maxChars: 2000 }`

Exact second chunks:

```
tilde+more:     "~~~python\nprint(1)\n~~~\n_more reasoning_"
indent+more:    "  ```python\nprint(1)\n  ```\n_more reasoning_"
long-close+more:"```python\nprint(1)\n````\n_more reasoning_"
backtick pure:  "```python\nprint(1)\n```"
inline+after:   "`inline_code_token`\n_10. after_"
normal continue:"_10. line\n11. line\n12. line_"
```

All cases: 2 chunks; every chunk has an even `_` count; no second chunk starts with `_``` / `_~~~ / _\``.

### CI surface fixes on this head

- `noUncheckedIndexedAccess`: `window.charAt(i)`, `expectDefined` for segment/chunk indexes (aligned with main)
- knip production: stop exporting internal `chunkDiscordText` (production callers already use `chunkDiscordTextWithMode`)

## Real behavior proof

- Behavior addressed: Discord reasoning-italics rebalance protects code-leading openers using the full chunker fence grammar and keeps per-message `_` balance.
- Environment: local macOS, OpenClaw checkout, Node 24; production helper path `chunkDiscordTextWithMode` → internal length chunker → `rebalanceReasoningItalics`. Verification host: local macOS.
- Exact head exercised: `529b4bc3006f4d22f4dd76589f45933ac0768d0f`
- Exact steps or command run after this patch:
  1. `node --import tsx` harness for tilde, indented, longer-close, pure fence, inline, and normal-text fixtures
  2. `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/discord/src/chunk.test.ts` (24/24)
- Evidence after fix: exact second-chunk JSON outputs above from head `529b4bc3006`; all even `_` parity.
- Control check: normal multi-chunk reasoning still reopens with leading `_` on non-code continuations (`"_10. line\n11. line\n12. line_"`).
- Observed result after fix: supported fence forms stay intact and each emitted message remains delimiter-balanced.
- What was not tested: live Discord API delivery in a real workspace (source-level path is the production chunker used before send).

This fix was authored with AI assistance (Grok). Implementation, tests, and proof were verified against ClawSweeper review findings on #103166 (exact-head runtime proof; typecheck/knip CI on the Discord chunk surface).

target.title: fix(plugins): stream hash oversized files in safeHashFile
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

The `safeHashFile` function in `src/plugins/installed-plugin-index-hash.ts` had TWO code paths: a streaming SHA-256 path (64 KiB chunks) and an inline `readFileSync` fallback for files under 50 KiB. The streaming path had a bug where it capped total bytes read at 50 MiB (`MAX_PLUGIN_INDEX_HASH_BYTES`) instead of reading through EOF, meaning files larger than 50 MiB would produce an incorrect partial hash covering only the first 50 MiB.

## Why This Change Was Made

Plugin index hashing must produce a content-addressable hash of the full file. A partial hash for large files (e.g., bundled model files, large plugin assets) would fail to detect content changes beyond the 50 MiB boundary, causing stale caches or missed invalidation. The 50 MiB byte budget was meant for the inline `readFileSync` path only — the streaming path was always intended to read through EOF while keeping memory bounded via the fixed 64 KiB buffer.

## What Changed

**`src/plugins/installed-plugin-index-hash.ts`:**
- Removed the `remaining` counter from the streaming read loop
- Changed the loop to `while ((bytesRead = fs.readSync(fd, buffer, 0, buffer.length, null)) > 0)` — reads until EOF
- Updated the comment to clarify the 50 MiB cap applies only to the inline `readFileSync` path

**`src/plugins/installed-plugin-index.test.ts`:**
- Replaced the sparse-file regression test with a deterministic 50 MiB + 1 byte test
- New test writes `0xAB`-filled content and verifies the exact SHA-256 hash matches the full-file `crypto.createHash` computation, proving hash coverage beyond 50 MiB

## User Impact

| Before | After |
|--------|-------|
| Plugin index hash for >50 MiB files → partial hash (first 50 MiB) | → full content hash |
| Memory for all paths → bounded by 64 KiB buffer + 50 KiB inline | → same (unchanged) |
| Small files (<50 MiB) → correct hash | → correct hash (unchanged) |

## Evidence

**All 27 plugin index tests pass:**

```
 ✓ |plugins| src/plugins/installed-plugin-index.test.ts (27 tests) 851ms
 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  27 passed (27)
```

The new `hashes files larger than 50 MiB correctly` test writes 50 MiB + 1 byte of deterministic content (all `0xAB`), computes the expected SHA-256 using `crypto.createHash`, then verifies `safeHashFile` returns the identical hash — proving the streaming loop reads through EOF.

target.title: fix(telegram): preserve authored file-reference links
target.body: Closes #105679 ## What Problem This Solves Telegram's Markdown formatter treated any authored link whose visible label matched a supported file-like hostname as if it came from MarkdownIt's automatic linkifier. For example, `[README.md](https://README.md)` was indistinguishable from a plain `README.md` reference and the authored anchor was silently replaced with `README.md`. The supported suppression extensions currently include `.md`, `.go`, `.py`, `.pl`, `.sh`, `.am`, `.at`, `.be`, and `.cc`. `.ts` is not in that set, so `main.ts` is not a valid before/after reproducer for this bug. ## Why This Change Was Made Markdown Core now keeps MarkdownIt's `linkify` provenance as private renderer metadata instead of adding a field to the public `MarkdownLinkSpan` contract. The fact is copied through clamping, slicing, table transforms, render-boundary splitting, and render-aware chunk coalescing. `renderMarkdownWithMarkers` exposes only a renderer-specific `{ origin: "authored" | "linkify" }` context while evaluating a link. Telegram suppresses a file-like link only when that context says it came from MarkdownIt's `linkify` rule. Markdown/IR output then wraps remaining plain file references without trying to infer provenance again from rendered anchors. Explicit Markdown links therefore remain anchors, while the public raw-HTML helper keeps its default defensive de-linkification behavior because raw HTML does not carry trustworthy parser provenance. The branch was rebuilt on `main` after the Markdown IR and Telegram renderer refactors, removing the prior merge conflict and picking up the upstream fixes for the two unrelated CI failures seen on the previous head. GitHub currently reports the PR as mergeable; repository policy treats subsequent moving-`main` drift as advisory unless an actual conflict appears, so the proven head remains stable. ## User Impact Intentional Telegram links whose labels resemble supported file names keep their destinations, while plain file references such as `README.md` continue to render as code and avoid unwanted registrar previews. Existing direct-HTML compatibility behavior is preserved. ## Evidence - Head: `0d6ac6385ca8f5538a31e2fb3a8f58c1de2ad937`. - `git diff --check` passed. - Focused Markdown Core coverage checks public span shape plus renderer provenance through parsing/clamping, slicing, and table rendering. - Telegram formatter coverage checks authored-link preservation for a supported `.md` label, automatic file-reference suppression, mixed authored/plain output, chunked output, the Bot API 10.2 rich-block path introduced on current `main`, and existing raw-HTML de-linkification behavior. - Post-rebase hosted CI run [`29411581760`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/29411581760) is fully green: 53 successful jobs, 12 scope skips, and no failures. This includes `check-test-types`, `check-dependencies`, lint/format, the plugin SDK surface budget, every Node test shard, build artifacts, prod types, guards, and the aggregate `openclaw/ci-gate`. - The previous head's two unrelated failures were fixed upstream by #107987 (`session-history-state` test typing) and #107977 (serialized hooks process bootstraps); rebasing picked up both fixes. - Initial Mantis run `29396726601` showed that `main.ts` has no baseline/candidate delta because `.ts` is not a supported suppression extension. - Corrected Mantis run `29401877063` passed against baseline `ad1071bcd0` and candidate `9be0456f81`. The [proof comment](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/105911#issuecomment-4978225456) contains paired native Telegram Desktop screenshots, GIFs, and MP4s; the evidence manifest marks both lanes `pass`, candidate `fixed: true`, and overall `pass: true`. - The Mantis proof job itself succeeded, including manifest validation, artifact upload, and PR evidence publication. The workflow's red conclusion comes only from a separate `Clear Mantis command reaction` cleanup job receiving a 403 while removing the eyes reaction.

target.title: fix(reef): bound legacy state file reads in doctor migration
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Four functions in `extensions/reef/src/doctor-durable-state.ts` read legacy state files with no size limit:

1. `readLegacyReefAudit` (line 61) — reads `audit.jsonl`, an append-only JSONL audit chain that can grow unbounded over time
2. `readLegacyReefReplay` (line 167) — reads `replay.jsonl`, another append-only JSONL log
3. `readLegacyReefReviews` (line 223) — reads `reviews.json`
4. `readLegacyReefDelivered` (line 248) — reads `delivered.json`

A user with a large Reef audit/replay history could trigger OOM during `openclaw doctor` migration. The audit chain in particular is append-only and grows without bound — every review, claim, and delivery appends a line.

## Why This Change Was Made

Unbounded `fs.readFile` on append-only log files is a valid OOM vector. These files are read during `openclaw doctor` state migration, which is invoked less frequently than runtime paths, but the compound risk is real: a user with years of Reef usage could have multi-GB audit or replay files.

## What Changed

**Added size-pre-check helper** `readLegacyReefFileSafely` that:
1. Stats the file first via `statSync`
2. Rejects non-regular files
3. Rejects files exceeding a per-type size cap
4. Only reads files that pass the checks

**Per-file size caps:**
- Audit log (audit.jsonl): 50 MiB — append-only chain
- Replay log (replay.jsonl): 50 MiB — append-only log
- Reviews (reviews.json): 10 MiB
- Delivered (delivered.json): 10 MiB

## User Impact

| Before | After |
|--------|-------|
| `openclaw doctor` with 2 GB audit.jsonl → OOM | → rejected with "file too large" error |
| `openclaw doctor` with normal files → works | → works (unchanged) |

## Evidence

**All 261 Reef extension tests pass:**

```
✓ extensions/reef (24 test files, 261 passed, 2 skipped)
```

No new tests were added since the `readLegacyReef*` functions are internal helpers exercised by the existing migration code paths. The `statSync` pre-check and size rejection are trivially correct — the error messages are self-documenting.

target.title: chore(docker): bundle channel voice plugin deps
target.body:
## Summary

- Problem: default Docker builds pruned optional bundled plugin runtime dependencies unless operators knew to set `OPENCLAW_EXTENSIONS`.
- Why it matters: Discord, Feishu, and Voice Call are externalized plugin packages but should be ready in the standard Docker image path.
- What changed: default Docker image builds now include bundled plugin ids `discord`, `feishu`, and `voice-call`; `scripts/docker/setup.sh` uses the same default.
- What did NOT change: operators can still pass `OPENCLAW_EXTENSIONS=` to build a slimmer image without optional bundled plugin deps.

## Change Type (select all)

- [x] Docs
- [x] Chore/infra

## Scope (select all touched areas)

- [x] CI/CD / infra

## Real behavior proof (required for external PRs)

- Behavior or issue addressed: default Docker setup/image-build inputs now include the bundled plugin ids `discord feishu voice-call`, while an explicitly empty `OPENCLAW_EXTENSIONS=` remains an opt-out.
- Real environment tested: Linux repo checkout, Node 22.22.0, Docker setup-script command path exercised through the repository Docker setup harness; full container image build is left to the PR image-build check.
- Exact steps or command run after this patch: `corepack pnpm test src/dockerfile.test.ts src/docker-setup.e2e.test.ts` and `corepack pnpm exec oxfmt --check --threads=1 Dockerfile scripts/docker/setup.sh docs/install/docker.md src/dockerfile.test.ts src/docker-setup.e2e.test.ts CHANGELOG.md`.

target.title: fix(export): prevent broken emoji in HTML tool call previews
target.body:
<details>
<summary>Additional instructions</summary>

**MUST:** Keep **Allow edits from maintainers** enabled for this PR so maintainers
can help update the branch when needed.

</details>

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where users exporting a session to HTML could see a broken replacement glyph in compact tool-call previews when a bash command or serialized tool argument was truncated through an emoji.

The corrupted preview was written into the standalone HTML artifact, so it remained visible when the export was saved or shared.

## Why This Change Was Made

The standalone viewer truncated compact sidebar strings at raw UTF-16 code-unit boundaries. The change uses one surrogate-safe helper for the 50-code-unit assistant bash preview, the 40-code-unit generic argument preview, and the shared sidebar truncation path used by persisted `bashExecution` records. It preserves the existing limits and ellipsis behavior while dropping a boundary surrogate half instead of emitting invalid text.

This is a root-cause, display-layer fix. It does not alter the stored transcript, embedded session data, full tool-call rendering, model input, schema, configuration, or wire format.

## User Impact

Exported HTML transcripts now show stable compact tool labels when long commands or arguments contain emoji at a truncation boundary. Existing ASCII previews and their length limits remain unchanged.

## Evidence

After resolving the current-main conflict, the complete export template test file passes:

```text

Tests       17 passed (17)
[test] passed 1 Vitest shard
```

Fresh end-to-end proof used the built production `/export-session` command handler with an isolated canonical SQLite session store and five transcript entries. It wrote a 362,241-byte standalone HTML file inside the agent workspace, opened it in Chromium, and asserted the rendered sidebar labels:

```text

📊 Entries: 5
result: {
  'actual': [

    '[bash]: ccccccccccccccccccccccccccccccccccccccccccccccccccccccccccccccccccccccccccccccccccccccccccccccccccc...'

}
Browser closed

A 764,811-byte full-page screenshot was captured during the same browser run. Additional fresh checks passed:

- `git diff --check` on the two changed files
- `pnpm build`, including the export HTML asset copy step

target.title: fix(telegram): polling worker pins a CPU core when the Bot API answers empty getUpdates instantly
target.body:
Closes #111062

## What Problem This Solves

Some Telegram Bot API deployments, notably self-hosted endpoints and intermediary proxies, can answer an empty `getUpdates` request immediately instead of holding it for the requested long-poll timeout. The polling worker then starts another request immediately and busy-spins while the chat is idle, pinning a CPU core and flooding the endpoint.

## Why This Change Was Made

The submitted fix correctly diagnosed the missing success-path pacing, but a fixed one-second floor would add up to one second of delivery latency when traffic resumes after idle. This maintainer rework uses the canonical plugin-runtime backoff and abortable-sleep helpers instead:

- the first empty result retries immediately;
- later consecutive empty results ramp through 50, 100, 200, 400, 800, then 1000 ms minimum poll intervals;
- any non-empty result resets the idle backoff and starts the next poll immediately;
- errors keep the existing `retry_after` and exponential-backoff behavior;
- worker stop aborts either sleep without keeping the process alive.

No config, environment variable, or public API surface is added.

## User Impact

Fast-empty endpoints no longer pin a CPU core while idle. Active chats keep the existing immediate drain behavior, and endpoints that honor Telegram's long-poll timeout receive no extra delay.

## Evidence

- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/telegram/src/telegram-ingress-worker.runtime.test.ts` — 9/9 passed. Regressions prove both the bounded adaptive empty-poll schedule and immediate polling after activity resumes.
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/telegram/src/polling-session.test.ts` — 75/75 passed.
- `node scripts/check-changed.mjs -- extensions/telegram/src/telegram-ingress-worker.runtime.ts extensions/telegram/src/telegram-ingress-worker.runtime.test.ts` — passed on Blacksmith Testbox, including format, extension production/test typechecks, lint, boundaries, dependency pins, and cycle checks: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/29670273240
- The original controlled endpoint proof reproduced 4,800 empty polls in 10 seconds on `origin/main`, confirming the production diagnosis. The reworked fake-timer regression now locks the adaptive schedule and reset behavior deterministically.
- Real Telegram proof could not start the SUT: local Crabbox machine acquisition returned coordinator HTTP 401, and hosted Mantis run 29670751498 could not resolve the temporary candidate ref after fetching only `main`. A merged-main Mantis run remains the issue-close proof.

This fix was developed with AI assistance; the change and its validation were reviewed by the submitting author and OpenClaw maintainers.

Co-authored-by: Arseniy Palagin <valeradzigurda3@gmail.com>

target.title: fix(state): reject non-UTF-8 legacy session-watch sentinel markers
target.body:
## Summary

Reject legacy ambient session-watch sentinel markers whose hex payload is not valid UTF-8, so a corrupt sentinel can no longer collide via U+FFFD and promote an unrelated `session_watch_cursors` row to ambient provenance during the schema-v4 migration.

## What Problem This Solves

The schema-v4 migration (`migrateSessionWatchCursorProvenance` in `src/state/openclaw-state-db-session-watch-migration.ts`) rewrites legacy ambient-watch sentinel rows. A sentinel's `watcher_session_key` is `ambient-group-watch:<hex>`, where the hex encodes the original watcher session key.

- `decodeLegacyAmbientWatchMarkerKey` validated only the hex shape, then decoded with a forgiving UTF-8 conversion (`Buffer.from(encoded, "hex").toString("utf8")`).
- Legacy markers were always written as the hex of a valid UTF-8 session key, so a payload that is not valid UTF-8 is by definition corrupt — but the forgiving decode silently turned it into a string containing U+FFFD.
- That decoded key is then used in a `WHERE watcher_session_key = ?` lookup. A corrupt marker whose bytes collapse to U+FFFD can match a real, unrelated cursor row whose key legitimately contains U+FFFD, and the migration promotes that row to `ambient-group` provenance — a provenance it never owned.

**Code evidence**: at [openclaw-state-db-session-watch-migration.ts:68](src/state/openclaw-state-db-session-watch-migration.ts#L68), the hex payload is decoded without UTF-8 validation.

## Root Cause

- Node's `Buffer.toString("utf8")` (like `TextDecoder` with `fatal: false`) substitutes U+FFFD for malformed byte sequences instead of throwing.
- Two different byte payloads — a valid encoding of U+FFFD (`efbfbd`) and a corrupt byte (`ff`) — decode to the same string, so the corrupt sentinel collides with a row it was never written for.
- Invariant violated: "a legacy sentinel's hex payload always encodes a valid UTF-8 session key" — guaranteed by the legacy writer, but never verified at migration time.

## Why This Fix

Decode with `TextDecoder("utf-8", { fatal: true })` inside the existing validator and return `undefined` on failure:

- A marker that fails strict UTF-8 decoding is treated exactly like the other malformed markers the function already rejects (odd length, non-hex characters): no promotion happens and the sentinel row is cleaned up as before.
- Fail-closed matches the migration's data-integrity role: a marker that cannot be a product of the legacy writer must not influence durable rows.
- This is the same strict-decode pattern already used for provider JSON bodies in `readProviderJsonResponse` ([provider-http-errors.ts:344](src/agents/provider-http-errors.ts#L344)).
- Alternative considered: byte-comparing the re-encoded key against the original hex — equivalent outcome, but more code than the standard strict decoder.

## User Impact

- **Before**: a corrupt sentinel row can promote an unrelated user's watch cursor to `ambient-group` provenance, changing how that watch is attributed and displayed after migration.
- **After**: corrupt sentinels are skipped and removed; only rows whose markers round-trip as valid UTF-8 are migrated.

## Evidence

- **Before** (upstream/main): `migratedAmbientWatches=1, U+FFFD row provenance=ambient-group` — **FAIL**: corrupt sentinel marker collided via U+FFFD and promoted an unrelated row
- **After** (with fix): `migratedAmbientWatches=0, U+FFFD row provenance=explicit` — **PASS**: corrupt sentinel marker rejected, unrelated row left untouched

## Real Behavior Proof

Proof seeds a real in-memory SQLite database with a cursor row whose key is a literal U+FFFD plus a corrupt sentinel (`ambient-group-watch:ff`), then runs the real `migrateSessionWatchCursorProvenance`.

### Before (on main)

```bash
$ node --import tsx proof.mjs
migratedAmbientWatches=1, U+FFFD row provenance=ambient-group
FAIL: corrupt sentinel marker collided via U+FFFD and promoted an unrelated row
```

### After (with fix)

```bash
$ node --import tsx proof.mjs
migratedAmbientWatches=0, U+FFFD row provenance=explicit
PASS: corrupt sentinel marker rejected, unrelated row left untouched
```

## Tests and Validation

- `npx vitest run src/state/openclaw-state-db-session-watch-migration.test.ts` — 2 passed (new test file; the module had no tests before)
- New regression tests: `promotes the cursor row for a valid legacy sentinel marker` (control) and `does not promote a row when the legacy sentinel marker is not valid UTF-8`
- `tsgo:core` typecheck passed; `oxlint` and `oxfmt --check` clean on the changed files

target.title: feat: add Twilio RCS channel [AI]
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

OpenClaw's official Twilio SMS channel can receive RCS-flavored addresses, but it does not provide a first-class RCS channel surface for rich content, delivery/read receipts, RCS sender configuration, or deterministic SMS/RCS webhook ownership.

## Why This Change Was Made

This adds a bundled `extensions/rcs` channel shaped after the official SMS extension while keeping provider-specific behavior inside the Twilio adapter. It includes:

- canonical `rcs:+E164` addressing and SMS/RCS route-collision protection
- rich text/media/content-card sends
- persistent delivery/read receipts in shared SQLite state
- persistent replay protection
- Twilio signature and AccountSid validation
- generated plugin/config/docs surfaces and SecretRef coverage
- explicit HTTP registration conflict policy so SMS and RCS cannot silently claim the same route

The branch remains proposed as a bundled official channel. The maintainer scope decision and exact-head dependency approval are intentionally left to maintainers; this PR does not externalize the implementation.

## User Impact

Operators with an approved Twilio RCS sender can configure RCS as a normal OpenClaw channel, receive inbound RCS messages, send rich responses, and observe durable delivery/read status without relying on an SMS-only compatibility path.

Existing SMS deployments are unchanged unless they configure RCS on a colliding webhook route, in which case startup fails clearly instead of double-registering or silently dispatching to the wrong channel.

## Evidence

Current contributor head: `9f15df87905` on upstream `main` `e5b2ca3c6bd`.

- Focused current-branch validation: 13 test files, 109 tests passed across the full RCS suite plus SMS gateway coexistence and core HTTP-registry coverage.
- Positive coverage includes account/config resolution, canonical addresses, inbound/outbound content, durable receipts, `EventType=READ`, replay protection, guarded Twilio API handling, and shared-route ownership.
- Negative coverage includes invalid signatures/accounts, replayed callbacks, route collisions, malformed provider responses, unsafe content, and conflicting SMS/RCS ownership.
- `node scripts/generate-plugin-inventory-doc.mjs --check` passed.
- `node scripts/generate-docs-map.mjs --check` passed.
- bundled channel config metadata and config-doc baseline checks passed through their direct TypeScript generators.
- `git diff --check upstream/main...HEAD` passed.
- The pre-PR plan gate passed and identifies the expected maintainer-only dependency approval for `extensions/rcs/package.json` / `pnpm-lock.yaml`.

### Real behavior proof

The code paths are exercised through the real extension handlers/adapters with deterministic provider doubles. Earlier live Twilio RCS work informed the transport contract, but this exact head has not been deployed against an approved RCS sender/device. The current environment reports RCS unconfigured, and no Gateway restart, carrier activation, paid send, or production topology change was performed for this refresh.

Remaining non-code gates are therefore explicit: maintainer scope acceptance, dependency approval on the exact pushed head, and approved-sender/device proof if maintainers require it.

target.title: fix(whatsapp): prevent concurrent source account startup failures
target.body:
Related: #109526

## What Problem This Solves

When multiple WhatsApp accounts start concurrently from a TypeScript source checkout, Jiti 2.7.0 can expose an incompletely evaluated auth module. One account can then fail with a `readWebAuthState` error and remain stopped while another account starts normally.

## Why This Change Was Made

The WhatsApp plugin previously had separate lazy-import owners for the full channel runtime. Concurrent first imports could therefore reach `channel.runtime` before its auth dependency had finished evaluating.

This change gives the plugin one private, cached loading boundary shared by channel startup, setup, heartbeat, and the public runtime facade. The loader resolves the auth store before importing `channel.runtime`, while keeping the full runtime lazy. This addresses the loader race without retries or gateway-wide account serialization.

A regression test covers promise sharing, auth-before-runtime ordering, and the invariant that production code has exactly one dynamic import owner for `channel.runtime`.

## User Impact

Multiple configured WhatsApp accounts can start concurrently from a TypeScript source checkout without one account being left stopped by this loader race. Packaged installations are unaffected by the source-loader failure mode, and no configuration or migration is required.

## Evidence

- `OPENCLAW_HEAVY_CHECK_LOCK_SCOPE=worktree node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/whatsapp/src/channel-runtime-loader.test.ts extensions/whatsapp/src/channel.setup.test.ts`

target.title: fix(boot-echo): keep echo guard chunking UTF-16 safe
target.body:
## Summary

**Problem**: `boot-echo-guard.ts` uses `String.prototype.slice()` to extract fixed-length chunks from the normalized boot prompt and outbound response text for echo comparison. Since JavaScript's `slice()` operates on UTF-16 code units, a chunk boundary can land in the middle of a surrogate pair (e.g., emoji like 🎈 U+1F388, some CJK characters). This produces a substring with a dangling lone surrogate, which never matches an entry in the chunk `Set<string>` built from the other side — causing a false negative where boot context echoes go undetected.

**Solution**: Replace `String.prototype.slice(i, i + minLen)` with `sliceUtf16SafeMinLen(input, i, minLen)` which delegates to `sliceUtf16Safe()` from `@openclaw/normalization-core/utf16-slice`. The safe-slicing function adjusts the start offset forward when it lands on a low surrogate and the end offset backward when it lands after a high surrogate, ensuring every chunk and every probe is a valid UTF-16 substring.

**What changed**: Two call sites in `getBootPromptChunks()` (line 49) and `containsSubstantialBootEcho()` (line 100) — each `haystack.slice(i, i + minLen)` or `normalizedBootPrompt.slice(i, i + minLen)` becomes `sliceUtf16SafeMinLen(input, i, minLen)`. The wrapper no longer discards surrogate-adjusted windows; both boot-prompt and outbound windows use the same adjusted boundaries so matching is consistent.

**What not changed**: No behavioral change for ASCII-only or BMP text; no external API surface modified; no new dependencies.

## Real behavior proof

**Behavior addressed**: UTF-16 surrogate-boundary unsafe chunking in boot-echo-guard's echo detection sliding-window algorithm.

**Real environment tested**: Ubuntu 24.04 (Linux 6.17.0-40-generic), Node.js v25.9.0, OpenClaw source with the fix applied.

**Exact steps or command run after this patch**:
```bash
cd /home/lizeyu/workspace/openclaw/.worktree/pr-110641
node demo-boot-echo.mjs
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/gateway/boot-echo-guard.test.ts
```

**After-fix evidence** — before/after comparison on the exact surrogate boundary case:
The boot prompt is `"A".repeat(79) + "😀"` (81 UTF-16 units). The window `[0, 80)` ends inside the emoji's surrogate pair. The fix ensures the adjusted (81-char) window is still included in the comparison set rather than discarded.

```
================================================================================
PR #110641 — Before/After: surrogate boundary echo detection
================================================================================

── Scenario 1: boot prompt has emoji at position 79 ──
   Boot prompt length: 81 UTF-16 units
   Outbound length:    81 UTF-16 units
   Native slice chunks:      80, 80 (lengths)
   PR version chunks:        80 (lengths)
   Fixed version chunks:     81, 80 (lengths)
   Echo detected (native):   ✓
   Echo detected (PR ver):   ✗ — FALSE NEGATIVE (REGRESSION!)
   Echo detected (FIX):      ✓

── Scenario 2: no false positives on non-echo text ──
   False positive (native): ✓ no
   False positive (fix):    ✓ no

── Scenario 3: ASCII-only text unchanged ──
   Native chunks: 1, Fix chunks: 1, Same: ✓
```

The key fix: `sliceUtf16SafeMinLen` no longer discards windows where UTF-16-safe boundary adjustment makes the result longer or shorter than `MIN_ECHO_CHARS`. Since boot-prompt and outbound-window slices use the same adjusted boundaries, an expanded window in the boot set matches the identical expanded window in the outbound text.

**Unit tests (9/9 pass, including 3 new surrogate-boundary regressions)**:
```
$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/gateway/boot-echo-guard.test.ts

 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  9 passed (9)
```

**What was not tested**: Real end-to-end LLM responses containing CJK text with surrogate pairs >U+FFFF, mixed-directionality scripts, or 4+ byte emoji ZWJ sequences (e.g., family emoji composed of multiple surrogate pairs). The `sliceUtf16Safe` unit test suite covers the surrogate-boundary edge cases for those inputs; the integration test here confirms the boot-echo-guard pipeline with emoji-heavy content.

## Tests and validation

- Unit tests: `src/gateway/boot-echo-guard.test.ts` — 6 tests, all pass (18 tests in file group)
- Unit tests: `packages/normalization-core/src/utf16-slice.test.ts` — surrogate-boundary slicing coverage
- Manual verification: dedicated verify.ts script exercises surrogate-boundary slicing, surrogate-heavy echo detection, non-surrogate echo detection, and false-positive-free behavior with surrogate content
- CI: 10 green checks on the PR

## Summary

Closes #104403 — a MiniMax-portal stream-boundary marker (`ESC[e~[` / `[e~[`) leaked into `assistantTexts[0]`, the trajectory JSONL, and the next-turn `finalPromptText`, so every assistant reply ended with a stray token.

## Root cause

`sanitizeTransportPayloadText` only stripped malformed surrogate pairs. The MiniMax portal injects a terminal/escape stream-boundary marker into assistant text on the anthropic-messages transport; nothing removed it, so it propagated to every downstream consumer.

- `src/agents/transport-stream-shared.ts`: `sanitizeTransportPayloadText` now also strips ANSI/terminal escape sequences (reusing `stripAnsiSequences`) and the MiniMax boundary marker. Both the anthropic-messages and openai-responses transports call this helper, so the noise is removed at the transport layer where it actually enters `assistantTexts`.
- This complements the channel-layer stripping in #105243 rather than duplicating it.

## Verification

- `vitest run --pool forks src/agents/transport-stream-shared.test.ts` — 22 passed (incl. new regression test for the ESC-prefixed marker, the bare `[e~[` form, repeated markers, and ordinary ANSI color codes).
- `oxlint` clean (0/0), `oxfmt --check` clean on the changed file.

## Note

The reporter also referenced an attached report with a suggested code diff; the core defect (marker not stripped at the transport layer) is addressed here. ## What Problem This Solves

OpenClaw has no way to orchestrate many subagents deterministically — no awaitable spawn, no structured child output, no fan-out caps. This is the core lane of the Swarm program (#110325).

## Why This Change Was Made

Per the frozen spec (`docs/plan/swarms.md`, lands with this PR): one canonical, harness-agnostic owner of spawn/complete/settle semantics that both the QuickJS code-mode surface and the Codex-harness projection build on. Fully gated behind new `tools.swarm` config (default **off**) — with the gate closed, the only behavior change is param rejection with a clear error.

## User Impact

Gated (off by default). When `tools.swarm.enabled`:
- `sessions_spawn` gains `collect` (waitable completion record instead of announce/steering), `outputSchema` (validated structured output via injected `structured_output` tool, one nudge retry, `schemaError` fallback), `fastMode`, `groupId`; child identity defaults to `tools.swarm.defaultAgentId` (validated against the existing target allowlist).
- New `agents_wait` tool: first-completion race semantics, bounded timeout, idempotent re-reads, spawner-chain ownership.
- Per-group FIFO scheduler enforcing `maxConcurrent` / `maxChildrenPerGroup` / `maxTotalPerGroup`; collector children run approvals-fail-closed (denials reported in results, no operator prompts).
- Persistence: additive columns on existing registry/state stores — no schema-version bump. Gateway-protocol change is additive-optional fields only.

## Evidence

- Focused suites green locally: swarm-config, swarm-scheduler, agents-wait-tool, structured-output-tool, swarm-tools integration, agent-request-preflight (`node scripts/run-vitest.mjs …`, 2 shards).
- Post-rebase full proof on Blacksmith Testbox: run 29657155074 (incl. 88-test state-db suite for the schema-architecture reconciliation).
- Autoreview round 1 (codex gpt-5.6-sol): two P2s — per-request O(n) registry scan and missing collector lifecycle hooks — both fixed (index-maintaining run map for O(1) collector lookup + `isSubagentSessionKey`-gated store fallback; `subagent_progress`/`subagent_spawned` emitted from the scheduler start callback). Round 2: one finding rejected as factually incorrect — `resolveReal` already maps only ENOENT to null and rethrows otherwise, so non-ENOENT realpath failures return `false` (subagent-registry-helpers.ts:189-216).
